title: Set 108

sentences.ko: 뒤뜰에 다 차려 놨는데 정오쯤 바람이 세져서 식탁보가 옆집 마당으로 날아가 버렸어. 결국 전부 차고로 끌고 들어갔지. 솔직히 안이 더 나았어. 서로 목소리 높여서 떠들 필요가 없었거든. 엄마는 아직도 우리가 너무 일찍 접었다고 생각하셔.
sentences.text: We had the whole thing set up out back and then the wind picked up around noon, so the tablecloth went into the neighbor's yard and we ended up dragging everything into the garage. And honestly it was better in there, because nobody had to yell over each other. My mom still thinks we gave up too early.

alts.text: Everything was all set up in the backyard, and then the wind kicked up around noon, so the tablecloth took off into the neighbor's yard and we wound up hauling it all into the garage. Honestly it was better in there, because nobody had to shout over anybody. My mom still thinks we bailed too soon.

We had everything arranged in the back yard, and then the wind picked up around noon, so the tablecloth blew into the neighbor's yard and we ended up moving it all into the garage. It was genuinely better indoors, as no one had to raise their voice over anyone else. My mother still believes we gave up too early.

sentences.note: **the wind picked up** 은 바람이 갑자기 세졌다는 뜻입니다. **we ended up dragging** 처럼 ended up 뒤에 ing 를 쓰면 원래 그럴 생각은 없었는데 결국 그렇게 됐다는 말이 됩니다.

sentences.ko: 5번가에 있는 그 집, 네 말이 거의 맞았어. 음식은 네가 말한 딱 그만큼 맛있었어. 그런데 문 바로 옆자리에 앉히는 바람에 나는 내내 코트를 입고 있었고 아내도 거의 못 벗었어. 안쪽 방은 원래 열어 두는 거야? 아니면 우리가 그냥 날을 잘못 고른 거야?
sentences.text: You were right about that place on Fifth, mostly. The food was every bit as good as you said it was, but they sat us right by the door, so I had my coat on the whole time and my wife barely took hers off. Is the back room usually open, or did we just go on a bad night?

alts.text: Okay, you were mostly right about that Fifth Street spot. Food was every bit as good as you said, but they stuck us right by the door, so I had my coat on the whole time and my wife barely got hers off. Is the back room normally open, or did we just pick a bad night?

You were largely correct about the restaurant on Fifth. The food was every bit as good as you said it was, but we were seated directly beside the door, so I kept my coat on the entire time and my wife scarcely removed hers. Is the back room usually open, or did we simply come on an unfortunate night?

sentences.note: **every bit as good as you said** 는 들은 만큼 정말 그대로 좋았다는 강조 표현입니다. **go on a bad night** 는 하필 안 좋은 날에 갔다는 뜻입니다.
sentences.situation: 친구가 추천한 식당 다녀와서 후기 말하기

sentences.ko: 언니네 집에 다녀온 뒤로 강아지가 방마다 나를 졸졸 따라다녀. 문을 닫으면 문 앞에 앉아서 낑낑대고. 우리가 또 떠나는 줄 아는 것 같아. 여행 가방이 아직 복도에 그대로 나와 있거든. 치워야 하는데 어차피 2주 뒤에 또 거기로 운전해서 내려가.
sentences.text: The dog's been following me from room to room ever since we got back from my sister's, and if I shut a door she sits outside it and cries. I think she's convinced we're leaving again, because the suitcase is still sitting out in the hall. I should put it away, but I'm driving back down there in two weeks anyway.

alts.text: Ever since we got home from my sister's, the dog won't leave my side, and if I close a door she just sits outside it and cries. I'm pretty sure she thinks we're taking off again, since the suitcase is still sitting out in the hall. I should put it away, but I'm heading back down there in two weeks anyway.

The dog has followed me from room to room ever since we returned from my sister's, and if I close a door she sits outside it and cries. I believe she is convinced that we are leaving again, because the suitcase is still sitting out in the hall. I ought to put it away, but I am driving back down there in two weeks regardless.

sentences.note: **following me from room to room** 은 이 방 저 방 졸졸 따라다닌다는 뜻입니다. 문장 끝의 **anyway** 는 어차피 그럴 거라서 상관없다는 느낌을 줍니다.

sentences.ko: 6년째 같은 미용사한테 같은 머리를 하고 있는데 이제 28달러야. 그것도 팁 주기 전 가격이고. 뭐라고 말할 수도 없어. 그 사람이 정한 게 아니라 가게가 정한 거니까. 그래서 요즘은 4주마다 가던 걸 6주마다 가는데, 갈 때쯤 되면 꼴이 좀 말이 아니야.
sentences.text: I've been getting the same haircut from the same woman for six years and it's twenty eight dollars now, and that's before I tip her. And I can't say anything about it, because it isn't her, it's the shop. So now I'm going every six weeks instead of four, and I look a little rough by the end of it.

alts.text: Same woman's been cutting my hair the same way for six years, and it's twenty eight dollars now, and that's before I tip her. And I can't really say anything, because it isn't her, it's the shop. So now I'm going every six weeks instead of four, and I look pretty rough by the end of it.

I have been getting the same haircut from the same woman for six years, and it is now twenty eight dollars, and that is before I tip her. I cannot say anything about it, because it is not her doing, it is the shop. So I now go every six weeks rather than every four, and I look somewhat unkempt by the end of it.

sentences.note: **that's before I tip her** 는 팁은 아직 포함되지도 않은 금액이라는 뜻입니다. **look a little rough** 는 몰골이 좀 헝클어져 보인다는 말입니다.

sentences.ko: 1월에 사워도우 한다고 재료를 다 사 놓고 빵은 네 덩이쯤 구웠나, 지금은 그 병이 냉장고 맨 안쪽에 처박혀 있어. 눈에 안 띄게. 어려워서 그만둔 건 아니야. 그냥 시간 맞춰 집에 있어야 하는 게 싫었어. 남편이 일주일에 한 번꼴로 이거 버려도 되냐고 묻는데 나는 계속 아직은 안 된다고 해.
sentences.text: I bought everything for the sourdough thing back in January, and I made maybe four loaves, and now the jar's just sitting in the back of the fridge where I don't have to look at it. It wasn't hard, that's not why I stopped. I just didn't want to have to be home at the right times for it. My husband asks about once a week if he can throw it out and I keep telling him not yet.

alts.text: I got all the sourdough stuff back in January, made maybe four loaves, and now the jar's just shoved in the back of the fridge where I don't have to look at it. It wasn't hard, that's not why I quit. I just didn't wanna have to be home at the right times for it. My husband asks about once a week if he can toss it and I keep telling him not yet.

I purchased everything for the sourdough project back in January, and I made perhaps four loaves, and the jar now sits at the back of the refrigerator where I do not have to look at it. It was not difficult. That is not why I stopped. I simply did not wish to have to be at home at the right times for it. My husband asks about once a week whether he may throw it out, and I keep telling him not yet.

sentences.note: **where I don't have to look at it** 은 보기 싫어서 눈에 안 띄는 곳에 두었다는 뜻입니다. **that's not why I stopped** 는 앞에서 말한 이유는 진짜 이유가 아니라고 미리 못 박는 말입니다.

reviewed: 1번 한국어: '바람이 세지는 바람에' 는 '바람'이 연달아 나와 읽을 때 걸린다. '바람이 세져서' 로 고쳤다.
2번 한국어: '안쪽 방은 원래 여는 거야?' 는 말이 덜 자연스러워 '안쪽 방은 원래 열어 두는 거야?' 로 고쳤다.
3번 casual: 마지막 문장이 text 와 글자까지 똑같아서 말투 차이가 없었다. 'heading back down there' 로 바꿔 구어 쪽으로 벌렸다.
5번 formal: 'It was not difficult, which is not why I stopped' 는 which 가 앞 문장 전체를 받아 '어렵지 않았다는 것이 그만둔 이유가 아니다' 로 읽힌다. 뜻이 어긋나므로 두 문장으로 나눴다.
